# The message comes back verbatim, stamped with server time

**Claim.** The posted message is echoed back exactly, alongside `dateSent`, the server's own clock. Every request field is optional — an empty body is a valid connectivity check and comes back with `message: null`.

Applies to: `~1echoes/post`

## Observed exchange

_The cheapest possible proof that the base URL, auth header and mode are right._

```http
POST /echoes

{
  "message": "Anybody out there?"
}

→ 200
{
  "message": "Anybody out there?",
  "dateSent": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "delayInMilliseconds": null
}
```

_No field is required. An empty body echoes back a null message._

```http
POST /echoes

{}

→ 200
{
  "message": null,
  "dateSent": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "delayInMilliseconds": null
}
```
